body:
### ESLint version

v10.5.0

### What problem do you want to solve?

ESLint added useful validation for `meta.languages` recently. when a configured rule does not support the active language, ESLint throws. That is good for catching accidental misconfiguration.

However, this creates a difficult problem for shareable configs from plugins that contain rules for multiple languages.

For example, [`eslint-plugin-unicorn`](https://github.com/sindresorhus/eslint-plugin-unicorn) has mostly JavaScript rules, but also some rules that support CSS, HTML, JSON, Markdown, or any language. Ideally, users could write:

```js
export default defineConfig([
	{
		files: ['**/*.js'],
		extends: [unicorn.configs.recommended],
	},
	{
		files: ['**/*.json'],
		plugins: {json},
		language: 'json/json',
		extends: [unicorn.configs.recommended],
	},
]);
```

And ESLint would apply only the Unicorn rules whose `meta.languages` match the active language.

Currently, that config throws because the same `recommended` preset also contains JavaScript-only rules. The plugin can work around this by generating separate recommended configs per language, but that means every multi-language plugin has to duplicate ESLint's language matching logic and maintain multiple preset variants.

### What do you think is the correct solution?

Would you consider an optin way for shareable configs to filter incompatible rules by `meta.languages`?

For example, something like:

```js
{
	files: ['**/*.json'],
	plugins: {json},
	language: 'json/json',
	extends: [unicorn.configs.recommended],
	filterRulesByLanguage: true,
}
```

The current strict behavior could remain the default. The opt-in would let plugin presets "just work" in mixed-language configs when the correct language plugins are installed, while still preserving `meta.languages` as the source of truth.

Please focus on the problem statement and not too much on the proposed solution. There may be better solution for this.

### Participation

- [ ] I am willing to submit a pull request for this change.

### AI acknowledgment

- [x] I did not use AI to generate this issue report.
- [ ] (If the above is not checked) I have reviewed the AI-generated content before submitting.

### Additional comments

I also cannot just put `files` inside `unicorn.configs.recommended` since JS-only globs would stop the preset from working for TypeScript users, while TS/non-JS globs would cause ESLint to start matching files that may not have the required parser or language plugin configured...

title: Change Request: Allow shareable configs to apply only rules compatible with the active language
